points.label: Action and response
points.left: Saul offers daughters while planning Philistine danger; Michal loves David, the bride-price is brought, and Saul’s fear continues.
points.right: Jonathan warns David and reasons with Saul; after Saul again throws a spear, Michal lowers David through a window and delays the pursuers.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places a marriage joins David to the house Saul uses against him inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places two members of Saul’s house preserve David from Saul inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Samuel 18:17–30 and 1 Samuel 19:1–17 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Battle, Fame, and Saul’s House” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Jonathan and Michal interrupt Saul’s violence

payload.tension: 1 Samuel 18:17–30 foregrounds a marriage joins David to the house Saul uses against him; 1 Samuel 19:1–17 foregrounds two members of Saul’s house preserve David from Saul. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
